analysis: Only the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift changed, so no production code, trust boundary or deployment setting is altered by this PR. Changes in the visible patch and head text: StubTokenizer gains a decodeTable (lines 146-147, 155); makeBridge gains a stopStringScope parameter passed to EngineV2Bridge (lines 443, 462); and new tests starting near line 847 cover scoped stop-string matching via EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence. The base units (L2458-3147) are largely unchanged context covering the SSD prefix-cache resident/L2 preflight, receipt isolation, paged KV and seeded-id tests. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the new stop-sequence tests at lines 847-899 are not visible in the head text supplied (head text ends at line 674). Relevant threats are T-041 and A-001. The visible tests exercise the cache properties that T-041 relies on: receipt-callback isolation per scope (scope-a vs scope-b), cacheSalt plumbing, a donation demand hint of 0 skipping the write, and receipt cleanup on cancel. Test code only strengthens regression coverage and adds no attack surface. The production behavior of the new stopStringScope and matchedStopSequence is outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot assess it. It is a stop-sequence matching feature with no apparent link to the prefix-cache, crypto or attestation boundaries, but the production change in EngineV2Bridge (likely in another batch) should be reviewed for stop-string handling and information leakage in the reported stop sequences.
